propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times, each invoking git config user.name via subprocess, consuming 47.79s and 59.54s respectively; author values are identical within an import and can be cached once at import start.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging 3,000 times (once per CREATE), each rescanning the same staging root with 375,876 owner checks totaling 15.94s, while earlier prepared items remain unpublished; only the first new-ticket in a batch requires a sweep.

Controlled A/B with identical state, 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, and 24 commits shows 60.8s improvement (77.9%) by replacing only git-config and sweep collaborators with side-effect-free logical equivalents, discriminating these mechanisms from event serialization or commit-count alternatives.

The locked contract (N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 commits, >=10x reduction, crash-resume, rollback) permits bulk-path amortization of redundant setup without modifying crash-safety semantics or per-write validation.
Interactive and direct writes must retain live author lookup and per-sweep behavior; any bulk optimization must be scoped and not leak across calls, threads, or sessions.
